headline_marked: [[Netherlands opposes US chip bill]] targeting ASML and Chinese chipmakers
headline: Netherlands opposes US chip bill targeting ASML and Chinese chipmakers
summary: The Dutch Trade Minister visited Washington to oppose the MATCH Act, a US bill that would bar Chinese chipmakers from accessing Western semiconductor equipment, heavily impacting ASML.
details: Dutch Trade Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma visited Washington this week to meet with US officials and oppose the MATCH Act. This proposed bill aims to bar Chinese chipmakers from accessing Western semiconductor equipment, a move that would significantly impact ASML.

ASML, based in the Netherlands, is Europe’s most valuable company and the world's sole maker of sophisticated lithography machines for cutting-edge AI chips. China currently accounts for 19% of ASML’s net system sales.

The MATCH Act would extend existing controls, adding curbs to ASML’s deep ultraviolet immersion machines. This is in addition to the long-standing ban on its most advanced extreme ultraviolet (EUV) tools reaching China.

The bill would relegate older-generation deep ultraviolet tools, first shipped a decade ago, as off-limits to China. The Dutch minister called his visit to Congress "exceptional," stressing the "very high stakes" for the Netherlands.
Introduced in April, the bill has not yet faced a full House or Senate vote. Bloomberg notes it would likely need to be folded into a larger legislative package to pass.

headline_marked: [[Global operation disrupts Amadey & StealC]] cybercrime tools, recovers 27M credentials & $47M
headline: Global operation disrupts Amadey & StealC cybercrime tools, recovers 27M credentials & $47M
summary: International authorities and private firms simultaneously targeted Amadey and StealC, two widely used cybercrime tools, recovering 27 million stolen credentials and $47 million in criminal assets.
details: "Operation Endgame," a global effort by international authorities and tech companies, has disrupted a major cybercrime "assembly line." The operation simultaneously targeted Amadey and StealC, two widely used malicious tools, leading to the recovery of 27 million stolen login credentials and $47 million in criminal assets.

Amadey is a malware-as-a-service platform used since at least 2018 to compromise devices and deliver ransomware and other payloads. StealC is an infostealer-as-a-service, designed to collect credentials, crypto wallets, authentication cookies, and specific files from infected systems.

Despite being separate tools, Amadey and StealC shared underlying infrastructure, a fact determined by Microsoft's AI analysis. This insight allowed Microsoft attorneys to use RICO statutes, treating both tools as part of a single conspiracy for simultaneous disruption.

The action resulted in the disruption of over 200 command-and-control servers and severed criminal control of more than 18,000 infected computers. Europol confirmed the recovery of 27 million stolen login credentials and the uncovering of $47 million worth of "crypto assets of criminal origin."

Other companies like ESET, Proofpoint, and IBM X-Force assisted in the operation. Europol also disrupted SocGholish, a malware loader linked to the Russian cybercrime group Evil Corp, cleaning infected WordPress sites and notifying affected parties.
